title: Whittier, the town under one roof
hook: An Alaskan town where almost everyone lives in one tall building.
peek: Whittier, Alaska, has a few hundred residents, and most of them live in a single 14-storey tower. The post office, police station and a shop share the building, and the only road in runs through a one-lane tunnel.
lede: Whittier sits at the head of a narrow inlet of Prince William Sound, about 100 kilometres from Anchorage. Fewer than 300 people live there year-round, and most of them have the same address. Begich Towers, a 14-storey block built for the US Army in the 1950s, holds flats, the post office, the police station, a small shop and city offices.

bullets.text: Whittier was built by the Army during the Second World War as a hidden supply port, chosen partly because low cloud and mountains made it hard to spot from the air.
An even larger Army building, once described as a city under one roof, stands empty nearby. It was abandoned in the 1960s and is now a well-known ruin.
The only road in is a tunnel about 4 kilometres long that cars share with trains. It has one lane, so traffic takes turns in each direction on a timetable, and it closes at night.
The school stands across the road from the tower, joined to it by a short underground passage. Children can get to class through the worst of the winter without stepping outside.
Whittier gets several metres of snow in a typical winter, along with strong winds off the mountains. Living, shopping and working under one roof is a practical answer to the weather.
